name: R01 regions-cache: the maximum is three entries
why: a second visible document loses one of its two keys: killed by the constants row and the four-key cache rows

name: R02 regions-cache: the maximum is five entries
why: a fifth key is kept: killed by the constants row and the fifth-key cache rows (the oldest must be scanned again)

name: R03 regions-cache: one entry is always kept
why: a megabytes-sized document loses its engine-aware key to its blind one: killed by the constants row and by the row of two scans over the whole budget

name: R04 regions-cache: three entries are always kept
why: the memory bound is not applied to the third entry: killed by the constants row and by the rows where three scans do not fit

name: R05 regions-cache: the budget is one character short
why: four scans that total exactly the budget are not all kept: killed by the row of four quarters

name: R06 regions-cache: the budget is one character long
why: killed by the constants row (the cache rows over the budget are over it by 2 characters, so only the stated value tells)

name: R07 regions-cache: the budget is halved
why: four quarter-budget scans are no longer kept: killed by the row of four quarters and the constants row

name: P01 promoted: an index of 0 or less is not guarded
why: EQUIVALENT: at 0 the rebuilt list is [entries[0], ...nothing, ...entries.slice(1)], the same entries in the same order as the copy, and still another array

name: P02 promoted: an index equal to the length is a hit
why: the entry at the length is undefined and goes first: killed by the row of an index past either end

name: P03 promoted: a negative index is a hit
why: entries[-1] is undefined and goes first, with the whole list after it: killed by the row of an index past either end

name: P04 promoted: only the first entry stays behind the hit
why: a hit on the third or fourth entry loses the entries between: killed by the policy rows for the third and last entry and by the seeded reference

name: P05 promoted: the hit is not moved
why: a hit never becomes the most recent: killed by the promoted rows and the cache row 'a hit promotes'

name: P06 promoted: the hit goes to the back
why: the cache drops what was just asked: killed by the promoted rows

name: A01 admitted: the new entry goes to the back
why: the cache drops what was just scanned: killed by every admitted row (slow: about 115 s, the multi-megabyte rows rescan their texts at every miss; the kill is a real one, 29 and 26 failing rows)

name: A02 admitted: the always-kept count is a floor of one fewer
why: a pair over the budget loses its second entry, or its first: killed by the row 'kept whatever their size'

name: A03 admitted: the maximum is exclusive
why: three entries are kept where four are allowed: killed by the row of four small entries and the cache rows of four keys

name: A04 admitted: the budget is exclusive
why: entries whose texts total exactly the budget are dropped: killed by the row of 4 x 25 = 100, the row of four quarters and the row of three that fit exactly

name: A05 admitted: dropping needs the maximum AND the budget
why: a fifth small entry is kept and a big third one too: killed by the fifth-entry row and the rows over the budget

name: A06 admitted: the total is not reduced as entries are dropped
why: once over the budget everything past the always-kept entries goes: killed by 'dropping the oldest is enough' and the row where the third stays

name: A07 admitted: the total leaves out the new entry
from: let total = held.reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.text.length, 0);
to: let total = entries.reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.text.length, 0);
why: the new entry's size is not counted (and then subtracted when the back is dropped): killed by the boundary rows (3 x 25 + 26, four quarters, one character over)

name: A08 admitted: the total counts entries, not characters
why: no entry is ever dropped for its size: killed by every budget row

name: A09 admitted: the newest entry is dropped, not the oldest
why: the entry just scanned is the one that leaves: killed by every row that drops an entry (slow: about 115 s, the multi-megabyte rows rescan their texts at every miss; the kill is a real one, 29 and 26 failing rows)

name: W01 scanEntry: a hit is not promoted
why: the cache is first-in first-out, not least-recently-used: killed by the cache rows 'a hit promotes' and 'a hit on the oldest and then on the next oldest'

name: W02 scanEntry: a miss replaces the whole cache
why: one entry, not four: killed by every cache row that asks a second key

name: W03 scanEntry: the render mode is not part of the key
from: (e) => e.engine === engine && e.mode === mode && e.text === text,
why: a knitr document asked under --no-execute is served the executing scan: killed by the option-line rows of the setup chunk (s343-cell-option-lines-rows.test.ts), not by the cache rows, which never ask a knitr mode

name: W04 scanEntry: the engine is not part of the key
from: (e) => e.engine === engine && e.mode === mode && e.text === text,
why: the blind and the aware scans of one text are one entry: killed by the cache rows (two keys, two scans) and the option-line rows

name: W05 scanEntry: the text is not part of the key
from: (e) => e.engine === engine && e.mode === mode && e.text === text,
why: another document is served the last scan: killed by every row that asks two texts

name: W06 scanEntry: the render mode is not normalised for engines that do not read it
why: a jupyter document asked under both modes takes two of the four slots, and any value of the mode is a key: killed by the cache row 'a mode that no engine but knitr reads is not another key'

name: T01 cache rows: a quarter of the budget is a fifth
why: four scans of a fifth total 80 percent of the budget and are all kept, so the 'one character over' row finds the oldest still there: the rows' sizes are live

name: T02 seeded reference row: the floor on steps that dropped an entry for its size is 100000
why: the floor is a real count of the draw

name: T03 seeded reference row: the floor on steps that held four entries is 100000
why: the floor is a real count of the draw

name: T04 cache rows: the flush pushes out two scans only
why: a recorded gap of the isolation, not of the cache: the rows scan four fresh keys before they ask anything, which evicts what an earlier row left, and each row uses its own tags; the longer flush is a safeguard for a row that asks fewer keys
